items.title: 53571_Mary Lou Williams oral history interview
items.q: I couldn't play Rachmaninoff and any of those things.

ctx.x: they've written and you have to play it then. So why should I want to play something somebody else has written? When I was a kid and my principal got all these teachers and all these things for me, I couldn't play Rachmaninoff and any of those things. I had to improvise in it. I couldn't play it the way the music was. I can't play music - when I'm reading, I have to improvise then. I hear it and see it, you know. I'm improvising then; I can't play it the way it's written. I never could play anything note for note…
